goal: Allow the owner of an existing short link to extend its expiry, and include the remaining time until expiry in the analytics (stats) response, without breaking existing behaviour.

functional.text: Owner can extend the expiry of an existing, non-deleted short link by supplying an additional duration in seconds, which is added to the current expiry. Exposed as POST /api/urls/{code}/extend using the same owner authorization mechanism as deactivation.
acceptance: POST /api/urls/{code}/extend with a valid owner credential and a positive additionalSeconds returns 200 and the body contains the new expiresAt equal to the previous expiresAt plus additionalSeconds.
The extend request for an unknown code returns 404.
A request with additionalSeconds missing, zero, negative or non-numeric returns 400 and leaves expiry unchanged.
A request with a missing or wrong owner credential returns the same status as deactivation does for that case (401/403) and leaves expiry unchanged.
A request that would make the total lifetime from now exceed 365 days returns 400 and leaves expiry unchanged.

functional.text: Extending behaves sensibly for links in special states: expired, deactivated, or having no expiry.
acceptance: Extending a link that has already expired but is not deactivated returns 200 and sets expiresAt to now plus additionalSeconds, after which GET /r/{code} redirects again.
Extending a deactivated link returns 409 (or the status deactivation conflicts use) and does not reactivate it.
Extending a link that has no expiry returns 409 and does not set an expiry.

functional.text: The stats response of GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics includes the remaining time until expiry, as an additive field.
acceptance: For a link with a future expiry, GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics returns 200 with remainingSeconds as a non-negative integer, equal to expiresAt minus now, rounded down.
For a link that is already expired, remainingSeconds is 0.
For a link with no expiry, remainingSeconds is null.
All fields that existed in the analytics response before remain present with unchanged names and types.

functional.text: Existing behaviour must stay backward compatible, and the new extend endpoint must not alter redirect, create, or deactivate semantics.
acceptance: GET /r/{code} for an active, unexpired link still returns the same redirect status as before and still counts the click.
After a successful extend, GET /api/urls/{code} returns the updated expiresAt.
POST /api/urls and the deactivate endpoint keep their existing request and response contracts.

nonFunctional: The extend endpoint responds within 200 ms at p95 under 50 concurrent requests, excluding network latency.
Concurrent extend requests on the same link must not lose updates: N concurrent extends of S seconds each result in total added time of N*S seconds, unless the maximum lifetime cap is reached.
assumptions: Assumed (no answer): the extend request specifies an additional duration in whole seconds (additionalSeconds) added to the current expiry, not an absolute timestamp.
Assumed (no answer): the maximum total lifetime from the current time is 365 days; requests exceeding it are rejected with 400.

Assumed (no answer): the owner is identified and authorized the same way the existing deactivation endpoint does (reusing its credential and its 401/403/404 behaviour); no new identity mechanism is introduced.
Assumed (no answer): the remaining time is exposed as remainingSeconds, an integer or null, added to the existing analytics response, computed from the server clock at request time.
Assumed (no answer): extending an expired but not deactivated link revives it from the current time; deactivated links cannot be extended.
Assumed (no answer): links without an expiry cannot be extended, since there is nothing to extend (409).
